title: Set up and solve a one-step context problem
subtitle: Linear equations in one variable · 16 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **16 of the official questions in Linear equations in one variable are this one** — 10 Easy, 4 Medium, 2 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:

- The question is a short story with a starting amount and a constant rate: a fee plus a monthly charge, a quantity that drops by a fixed amount per time period, a perimeter with known sides, or a budget split between two purchases.
- It asks 'how many', 'after how many months/hours/days', or 'what is the length'.
- The answer is a single number.

sections.heading: The method
body: - If the rate isn't given, find it first by dividing the change between two data points by the time between them.
- 3) Reread what's being asked: total time or additional time, the item count or the dollars.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Graph y = start + rate·x and y = target, then click the intersection.
This is useful when the numbers are messy decimals.
For rate-from-two-points problems, you can enter the two points in a table and use a regression.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You answer a different quantity than the one asked: the extra hours instead of the total hours, the amount removed instead of the time, or the spending on one item instead of the count.
You also forget to subtract the one-time fee or starting amount before dividing.
